item.title: Family Sues Google Over Teenager’s Suicide-Related AI Chats On School Computer
item.description: The parents of a 13-year-old girl have sued Google claiming she planned a potential suicide and funeral using its AI technology on a school-issued computer. Filed Monday in a California court, the complaint is the first known case accusing Google of negligence related to AI integrations on Chromebooks, the tech giant’s low-cost laptops used by millions of students in the United States and around the world. The teenager, identified by the name Emma, was not able to access Google’s Gemini app, nor OpenAI’s ChatGPT, because they were blocked by her school. She was nonetheless still able to use Google’s search engine, which contains AI-powered tools. Those features were notably not among the tools that Google announced this week will be disabled by default for students. Google on March 21, 2023 invited people in the United States and Britain to test its AI chatbot, known as Bard, as it scrambles to catch up with Microsoft-backed ChatGPT. (Photo by Pau BARRENA / AFP) “Schools should turn search off and keep it off until Google removes AI mode from search or ensures that every single student is always safe when they’re interacting with AI,” Andrew Liddell, one of the family’s attorneys, told AFP on Thursday. The complaint alleges that Emma had been a “happy 13-year-old girl” in North Carolina who received great grades, played music and participated in Girl Scouts. Despite “no history” of mental illness, within months of using Google’s AI-powered search on her school laptop, she began a “quiet spiral into a severe psychological crisis” according to the complaint. On March 17, the school’s monitoring software flagged a document titled “Funeral,” and the school notified her parents. Her mother then saw Emma writing a farewell letter in real-time after logging into her daughter’s account, and her father intervened. “We are reviewing the claims in the lawsuit and we take this very seriously,” Google spokesperson Jose Castaneda told AFP. Google argues that AI mode includes safeguards against self-harm and attempts to bypass them. But Emma “was able to keep going back over and over and over again,” Liddle said. “Whatever safeguards they think they put in place were obviously insufficient.” Developers of fast-evolving AI technology are facing a litany of similar lawsuits in the US. OpenAI faces several wrongful death suits, including from the parents of 16-year-old Adam Raine, a teenager who committed suicide allegedly using methods advised by ChatGPT. Google and the startup Character.AI agreed in January to settle several lawsuits filed by families of teenagers out of court. On Wednesday, Google, TikTok and Meta each separately sued California to block a law that prohibits social media companies from providing addictive features to users under 16. Governor Gavin Newsom signed the law in September, and it goes into effect on January 1, 2027. item.title: ‘Too early for him’: Sachin Tendulkar's blunt verdict on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s leadership role at 15
item.description: At just 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already achieved milestones that remain a distant dream for many cricketers throughout their careers. From finishing as the leading run-scorer in an Indian Premier League (IPL) season to smashing a match-winning century in the U-19 World Cup final to clinch the title, the teenager has made remarkable strides in a short span of time. However, his elevation to the role of East Zone vice-captain for the Duleep Trophy did not go down well with everyone. Among those who believe the youngster was handed a leadership responsibility too early is batting legend Sachin Tendulkar. Although Tendulkar had not publicly questioned the selectors' decision at the time of the announcement, he shared his reservations during a Reddit Q&A session, suggesting that Sooryavanshi should focus on gaining more experience in red-ball cricket before taking on such responsibilities. Responding to a fan who asked for his views on the 15-year-old being entrusted with a leadership role, Tendulkar said: "I feel it's too early for him to become a vice-captain in the Duleep Trophy. We have to let him play more matches with the red ball and take one step at a time!" Sooryavanshi had featured in just eight red-ball matches for Bihar before being named East Zone skipper Ishan Kishan's deputy. The decision meant he was preferred over Abhimanyu Easwaran, an experienced campaigner with more than 100 First-Class appearances. The East Zone selection committee subsequently clarified that the appointment was made with the youngster's development in mind and should not be interpreted as an indication of the pecking order within the squad. Sooryavanshi also got a taste of captaincy during the tournament when Kishan was forced to leave the field due to an injury. The teenager stepped in to lead the side and was involved in several important on-field decisions, including DRS calls. Videos of his involvement in those reviews also gained traction on social media. Meanwhile, Sooryavanshi has continued to strengthen his position in India's T20I setup, although he is yet to establish himself as a regular opener. The youngster faces competition for a place in the top three from established names such as Sanju Samson, Abhishek Sharma and Ishan Kishan. Tendulkar names favourite captains During the same interaction, Tendulkar also reflected on his own stint as India's captain, describing the opportunity to lead the national side as a tremendous honour. However, he admitted that the position did not always give him complete control over team selection. Tendulkar, who made his international debut on November 15, 1989, before bringing the curtain down on his career on November 16, 2013, also spoke about the changes in the functioning of Indian cricket over the years. "It was a great honour to lead the team as captain. However, I didn’t always have the freedom to pick my team entirely on my own. The BCCI today is a far more professional organisation than it was in the 199

item.title: Bayern assistant Danks: Kompany recovering well but no return yet
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany (R) and assistant coach Aaron Danks walk across the field ahead of the German Bundesliga championship trophy ahead of the German Bundesliga soccer match between Bayern Munich and VfB Stuttgart at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Bayern assistant Danks: Kompany recovering well but no return yet») Tom Weller/dpa Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany is making progress in his recovery ahead of the team's away match in Mainz, assistant coach Aaron Danks said at a press conference on Friday. Danks could not yet say whether the 40-year-old Belgian could resume his role as coach of the German football record champions after his collapse two weeks earlier and a bout of meningitis following the international break. "I've had a few really good phone calls with Vince. He seems very positive and appears to be well on the way to a full recovery," Danks said. The assistant coach added that no date has been set yet for Kompany's return. "The international break provides a good opportunity to reflect and see when he can return," he said, adding that everyone hopes that it will be as soon as possible. Under the guidance of Kompany's assistant Danks, Bayern have won three and drawn one of their last four competitive matches. Another win could follow on Saturday in Mainz, where Bayern suffered their last away defeat, a 2-1 loss in December 2024. Since then, Bayern have gone 30 away matches unbeaten, recording 22 wins and eight draws. "We've got an important match on Saturday, and we want to round off this run with a good result. But it won't be easy. We know that," Danks said. Four days after the 2-0 Champions League win at Atlético Madrid, there could be changes to the starting line-up. "With a few players we need to look at workload and whether we rest them," Danks said. Danks named Alphonso Davies, who still needs rest periods after several injuries, and said he could not play 90 minutes in a row several times. Germany international Jamal Musiala is back in team training after his muscle injury. "But tomorrow's game comes too soon for him," Danks added.

item.title: Audrey Shindelar shines in SDSU debut, sets program debut scoring mark
item.description: South Dakota State true freshman Audrey Shindelar poured in 15 points on Tuesday, Nov. 2, setting the program's Division I record for points in a debut outing. Shindelar scored her 15 points in 22 minutes, going 7-for-11 from the field and 1-for-3 from three. She looked confident getting to her shot in both the half-court and on the break. "I trust my preparation and my teammates and coaches, I knew they had my back," Shindelar said. "I went in the game with confidence in what we had been working on." The freshman guard isn't normally a nervous person, but she was feeling the pressure a little before her first collegiate game. She was able to channel that positively and give her team a lift. "I'm not usually a very nervous person, but being in a new setting and in a little bit of the unknown," Shindelar said. "Before games there's just a different schedule and that kind of stuff. Then a lot of people were there supporting. It was really cool and it was good nerves." Shindelar's coaches and teammates weren't at all shocked at her performance. Shindelar is the all-time leading scorer at Stewartville High School in southeast Minnesota. She was also a Miss Basketball finalist in Minnesota a year ago. "Honestly, we're not surprised," SDSU guard Emilee Fox said after Tuesday's game. "Audrey's a really good player and we're really excited to see how she can progress each and every game." Head coach Aaron Johnston expected her to come in and contribute immediately, and is happy his freshman guard is succeeding early. He's going to be sure he isn't adding too much pressure to Shindelar as she continues getting adapted to the grind of a college season. "You never know how freshmen are going to jump into things," Johnston said. "It's hard going from a senior in high school to the freshman year in college against our level of competition. We want to make sure we don't put too much on her, but she's going to be a big part of what we do from Day 1 and going forward because she has the ability to create shots and has really good bounce in her step. She's going to be a great talent for us." Shindelar is hoping her opening performance can carry on in the season. She's just hoping that will result in some team wins after the Jackrabbits lost to Creighton at the buzzer. "The loss was tough, but I feel like consistency is a big part for everybody," Shindelar said. "I feel like that's an important piece in getting better every day in practice, every game." This article originally appeared on Sioux Falls Argus Leader: Audrey Shindelar shines in SDSU debut, sets program debut scoring mark

item.title: Ducks land in CFP rankings despite rocky season
item.description: Oregon football’s season hasn’t worked out the way it expected. But the Ducks (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten) were ranked in the first College Football Playoff rankings. Oregon came in at No. 23 in the initial rankings, revealed live on ESPN on Tuesday. Dan Lanning’s team is on the outside looking in at the 12-team playoff, one season before a 24-team playoff is set to likely go into effect. The No. 23 Ducks are coming off a confidence-boosting win over Northwestern, heading on the road to face No. 12 Ohio State (6-2, 4-1) this Saturday. That matchup originally included the preseason Nos. 1 and 2 teams in the AP poll. But in this chaotic college football season, the Buckeyes are reeling after a road loss to No. 20 USC. Other Big Ten teams in this week’s CFP rankings include No. 19 Iowa, No. 8 UCLA and No. 4 Indiana. item.title: NWSL playoff predictions: who can spoil Gotham’s bid for the double?
item.description: Rose Lavelle (Gotham), Croix Bethune (Kansas City) and Trinity Rodman (Washington) are among the stars seeking to lead their team to an NWSL title. Composite: Photo by Elsa/NWSL via Getty Images; Lachlan Cunningham/NWSL via Getty Images; Greg Fiume/Getty Images The regular season was defined by … Compelling storylines that kept the league interesting during a crowded sports summer. The interval years that aren’t Olympic or World Cup years are often quieter for the NWSL (see: average attendance was essentially flat among the non-expansion teams). In a year with the men’s World Cup on home soil and a major anniversary season for the WNBA, most of the NWSL’s teams gave a solid showing, with close competition for the Shield, an entertaining Golden Boot race and the returns of several big stars. Even those teams who did not give a solid showing – hello, Chicago – finally made some encouraging moves in the right direction. (Louisville next, please.) Ella Brockway The league working to gauge the heart of its fanbase. Recent weeks have seen contentious scenes, especially in Portland, as transphobic organizations try to work into the league discourse as they have with the WNBA. But beyond that, there have been considerable innovations made with an eye on garnering more attention. The “Rodman Rule” was hurried to production in part to keep arguably the most marketable US player from going abroad. The league briefly considered following MLS’s lead and inverting its schedule, only for a vote to be spurned after initial backlash from players and the public. It even got a feature in Ted Lasso. These efforts take time, but that’s a lot of willingness to change just about anything about the league’s structure if it moves the needle. Jeff Rueter Races to the top – and the bottom. The competition for both the Shield and Golden Boot was fierce. Ashley Sanchez pulled ahead for the Boot, but Barbra Banda, Sophia Wilson, Janine Sonis and Trinity Rodman provided some real fireworks. (Had Banda not been kept out of the country for the last month of games due to federal travel policies, she may have given Sanchez a run for her money.) The Shield race was even tighter, with three teams still in contention with two matches to go. However, the league struggled to maintain that quality across the board. Chicago, Louisville and Bay FC were embarrassingly bad – and boring – throughout the season. It’s a story that is too familiar, and doesn’t seem poised to change in a real way any time soon. As much as the league’s marketing centers parity, its choices prioritize expansion. With two new clubs arriving in 2028 and more on the way after, I worry the talent across the board will continue to be watered down, especially as the league’s salary cap and low minimum salary drives elite players away to teams in Europe, Mexico and Brazil. The NWSL will have to contend with what growing pains are inevitable, and which should really be avoided. Abigail Segel Related: Goals, guests and 6,5

item.title: Kimi Antonelli on Having His Dad at ‘99% of the Races’ as Life ‘Changed Drastically’
item.description: When you become the youngest Formula 1 World Champion in history at just 20 years old, it is terrifyingly easy to lose your grip on reality. Replacing a seven-time champion at Mercedes , dominating the grid, and suddenly becoming the most famous athlete in Italy is the kind of explosive spotlight that can completely break a young driver. So, how did Kimi Antonelli manage to keep his head screwed on straight while the F1 circus went into absolute overdrive around him? He brought his dad to work. Speaking with Anthony Davidson on the Nu Silver Arrows Radio Show , Antonelli peeled back the curtain on his inner circle. When asked who helped him survive the immense pressure and the difficult moments of his early career, the Mercedes star immediately pointed to his father, Marco Antonelli. Marco is no stranger to the brutal realities of the motorsport ecosystem. As a former racing driver himself and the boss of the AKM Motorsport outfit, he understands exactly how toxic the paddock can get. Having that veteran presence in his corner was the ultimate cheat code for the young champion. “First of all, my family, of course my dad, my mom, but my family in general, because they’re the ones who know me the best, inside out, and they’ve always been there for me, especially my dad coming to the races,” Antonelli explained. Antonelli on Surviving the “Drastic” Fame While Antonelli has projected an icy, unshakable composure inside the cockpit of the W17 this season, he didn’t sugarcoat the psychological toll of the 2026 campaign. Going from a highly touted rookie to a global superstar essentially overnight completely upended his normal reality. He heavily relied on his father to act as a shield against the paddock noise. Mexico City Grand Prix, Sunday MEXICO CITY, MEXICO – NOVEMBER 01: 2026 F1 World Drivers Champion and third placed Andrea Kimi Antonelli of Italy and Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team celebrates with his family in parc ferme during the F1 Grand Prix of Mexico at Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez on November 01, 2026 in Mexico City, Mexico. (Photo by Simon Galloway/LAT Images) “I know I can rely on him any time. That has made a difference even this year,” Antonelli confessed. “This year, having my dad there 99% of the races has been massively helpful, because it’s been such a big year for me so far that I needed that support from him to cope with all the different situations, to cope as well with all these high moments, because life has changed drastically as well this year”. Time to Go Home The relentless pace of the modern F1 calendar means Antonelli hasn’t actually had a second to breathe since clinching the title in Mexico. The paddock immediately packed up and flew directly to Interlagos for the Brazilian Grand Prix. With the constructor’s battle still raging, the 20-year-old is locked in for the São Paulo weekend. item.title: Why Soccer’s Major Tournaments Are Rethinking Opening Acts
item.description: HOUSTON, TEXAS - JULY 6: Edson Alvarez of Mexico and Guillermo Ochoa of Mexico lift the Gold Cup trophy with team mates during the Gold Cup 2025 Final match between United States and Mexico at NRG Stadium on July 6, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images) Getty Images For years, the traditional opening stages of major soccer tournaments have followed a familiar script: Group-stage games, a handful of predictable mismatches and the gradual build toward the heavyweight encounters that everyone really wants to see. That approach is changing. From UEFA’s revamped Champions League (now in its third year) to the significant restructuring of the 2027 CONCACAF Gold Cup, the game’s governing bodies are rethinking how their competitions begin with a common objective: Get the biggest teams playing more meaningful games against one another earlier in the tournament. There are differences between the Champions League and Gold Cup approaches. Nonetheless, both are responding to the same challenge: Making the opening stage feel like an essential part of the tournament rather than an obstacle to the games that really matter. The traditional group stage was designed around simplicity and familiarity. Instead, these newer models are designed around variety, competitive incentives and commercial appeal. Overall, the thinking is straightforward. Why make fans wait until the knockout rounds to see the most compelling matches when those games can become part of the opening act? The most prominent example is the Champions League, which introduced its expanded league-phase format in the 2024-25 season. Gone was the familiar arrangement of 32 clubs divided into eight groups of four, with each team playing three opponents twice. In its place came a 36-team competition in which every club plays eight different opponents – four at home and four away – in one overarching league table. The change was designed to produce more variety, more competitive balance and, crucially, more heavyweight encounters during the fall. That means supporters can see some of Europe’s biggest clubs take on each other ahead of the knockout stage. It also creates a more compelling competitive landscape, with every result affecting a shared table. There is also considerably more at stake throughout the opening phase. The top eight teams qualify directly to the round of 16, while clubs finishing between ninth and 24th enter a two-legged playoff. Those finishing 25th or lower are eliminated. As a result, the league phase is not simply an extended qualifying exercise. A team’s position can determine whether it enjoys a direct route to the last-16. UEFA’s experiment has now provided a template that other competitions are beginning to examine, although not necessarily an exact replica. item.title: How 14-Game Road Nonleague Schedule Benefits Mississippi Valley State
item.description: Former University of Albany forward Tarique Foster now plays at Mississippi Valley State, which is playing each of its 14 nonconference games on the road. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) Getty Images Mike Davis isn’t naïve. The first-year men’s basketball coach at Mississippi Valley State University knows his team is facing a challenging first two months of the season, maybe more so than any program in the nation. The Delta Devils are last among 365 Division 1 teams in analyst Ken Pomeroy’s ratings. Still, MVSU is playing each of its 14 nonconference games on the road, starting with Friday’s opener at Oklahoma. The Delta Devils face five teams that were in the 2026 NCAA tournament and four that are ranked in the Associated Press preseason poll in No. 4 Connecticut, No. 12 Arkansas, No. 16 Michigan and No. 19 Texas Tech. KenPom projects MVSU will lose each of the nonleague games by at least 21 points. And that doesn’t bother Davis. Not at all. In fact, Davis assembled the schedule soon after he took over MVSU in early May. The reasoning is two-fold. MVSU expects to earn about $1.5 million in revenue by playing these games, a massive figure for a school of its standing in the low-major Southwestern Athletic Conference. The Delta Devils also can test themselves against high-major programs, which may help them in conference play. During the 2024-25 school year, the most recent data available, MVSU’s athletics department generated $5.58 million in revenue, including $993,877 from the men’s basketball team, per the U.S. Department of Education’s database. By playing a difficult schedule, the men’s basketball team can add significant funds to the school’s financial coffers because major conference teams pay appearance fees to smaller schools that travel to their arenas. MVSU will receive an average of $110,000 per game for its nonconference games this season, according to athletics director Alecia Shields-Gadson. For instance, UConn is paying MVSU $115,000 for the Dec. 8 game at the Huskies’ on-campus Gampel Pavilion and providing the Delta Devils 25 complimentary tickets behind their bench, per terms of the contract obtained via an open records request. Oregon is paying MVSU $100,000 and providing 50 tickets for the game on Nov. 11, per the contract between the schools. And Michigan, the reigning national champion, is paying MVSU $95,000 and providing up to 75 tickets for the game on Dec. 1, according to the agreement. The money will help put the Delta Devils on more solid footing. Jerryl Briggs, MVSU’s president, has vowed that the school will share some of the revenue generated from the appearance fees with players, the first time that has happened. “It’s a great opportunity to be able to go out and recruit top talented kids and ensure that we can create a winning atmosphere,” Shields-Gadson said. “This is an exciting time, but we won’t have such an aggressive schedule every year. We wanted to do it this year to give some great exposure for

item.title: It's Now Or Never For This Cleveland Cavaliers Core
item.description: CLEVELAND, OHIO - SEPTEMBER 28: (L-R) Evan Mobley #4, Donovan Mitchell #45, James Harden #1 and Jarrett Allen #31 of the Cleveland Cavaliers laugh during Cleveland Cavaliers Media Day at Rocket Arena on September 28, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) Getty Images In mid-October, ESPN’s Zach Kram published his latest NBA Now or Later rankings , which gauge the teams that are under the most pressure to win right away. The rankings are based on how much money each team has tied up moving forward and their future first-round picks (or lack thereof). The Phoenix Suns led the way, as they’ve traded away four fully unprotected first-round picks over the next seven years and have given up swap rights in 2028 and 2030 as well. But the Cleveland Cavaliers were right behind them at No. 2 overall in ESPN’s rankings. The Cavs aren’t as overleveraged as the Suns in terms of future draft capital. They already owe their fully unprotected 2027, 2029 and 2031 first-round picks to other teams, and they’ve given up swap rights in 2028 as well. But for now, they have full control over their 2030, 2032 and 2033 first-rounders, whereas Phoenix only has control over its 2032 pick. What the Cavs don’t have is financial flexibility moving forward. The Suns have Devin Booker locked up on a 35% max contract, but they don’t have any massive long-term commitments beyond that. The Cavaliers can’t say the same. They just signed Donovan Mitchell to a 35% max deal, have Evan Mobley entering the second year of a 30% max and signed James Harden to a three-year, $96.5 million contract and added Peyton Watson on a four-year, $88 million deal via sign-and-trade this offseason. Throw in Jarrett Allen, who’s beginning a three-year, $90.7 million contract this season, and the Cavaliers have five players earning at least $20 million, three earning at least $30 million and two earning $50.1 million each. Next year, Mobley and Mitchell are projected to earn roughly $115 million combined, while Harden and Allen account for another $62.4 million. That quartet alone will push the Cavs over the 2027-28 salary cap, which is currently projected to land at $176 million . That’s setting this up to be a make-or-break season for the Cavaliers. If they fall short of the NBA Finals yet again, they may find it financially unsustainable to keep this core together moving forward. Can This Cavs Core Break Through? Eight games into the 2026-27 season, the Cavs have already shown a few red flags. In their season opener, they jumped out to a 29-point first-half lead over the Philadelphia 76ers and still managed to lose. They also lost a pair of games to the injury-ravaged Oklahoma City Thunder in early November even though OKC was without starters Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace and Chet Holmgren

item.title: Can MLS Capitalize on Son-Mania?
item.description: As Son Heung-min’s last-minute strike kissed the post and bounced agonizingly away in LAFC’s 1–1 draw with New York City FC on October 17, the assembled crowd at Citi Field let out a collective groan. Although it was technically a home match for the New York-based club, the seats around the makeshift soccer field were filled with fans wearing South Korea and Tottenham Hotspur shirts. The crowd reached a fever pitch every time Son touched the ball, hoping South Korea’s all-time top scorer could work another moment of magic at the tail end of his illustrious career. “He makes me very proud to be Korean,” Paul Oh, a Seoul-born fan donning a South Korea kit who now lives in New York City, told Front Office Sports at Citi Field. “He’s just a great player; he has such a great personality, he loves his fans, and you can feel that from him.” MLS is, in many ways, built on the Son formula. David Beckham’s global stardom helped launch the league into the mainstream between 2007 and 2012, and Lionel Messi has made Inter Miami matches the hottest ticket in town since joining the club in 2023. Son’s arrival at LAFC—alongside former Tottenham teammate Hugo Lloris—has taken that experience to a new level, and one that has divided MLS fans. Tottenham supporters clubs are now organizing trips to see the man who starred for their club for a decade play for LAFC. In August, the Washington, D.C.-based Tottenham supporters group DC Spurs hosted an event titled “Captains in the Capital” in conjunction with LAFC’s visit to D.C. United. Named for Son and Lloris, both former Tottenham captains, the event featured a watchalong of a Tottenham match at a bar and a group march to Audi Field for the MLS match. Over 900 fans attended the match through the event after D.C. United provided DC Spurs a group ticket package, and the team and supporters club collaborated to donate a portion of the proceeds to local educational nonprofit DC Scores. Not everyone was pleased with the initiative. After DC Spurs posted on Instagram advertising the event, D.C. United fans filled the comment section with disapproval. “Supporters group completely unaffiliated with any of the teams participating in the match is marching against the team from their city,” one fan wrote. “Support your local,” two other fans chimed in. DC Spurs defended itself in the comment section, saying the outing was “not about supporting LAFC or rooting against D.C. United.” “We encourage everyone to celebrate our former Spurs players while also showing respect and support for our local club,” DC Spurs wrote. Eric Kmetz, a treasurer and board member of DC Spurs, told FOS he hoped attending the match would inspire Spurs fans to become more involved with their local club. He cited a post-event survey the group conducted that showed more than half of respondents would attend another D.C. United match. “If we have gotten just one person to end up starting to support D.C. United as a result of going to the event, I view that a

item.title: SPL boss makes damning observation about Man United’s Jekyll and Hyde performance vs AS Roma
item.description: SPL boss makes damning observation about Man United’s Jekyll and Hyde performance vs AS Roma Dundee manager Steven Pressley has revealed what he told his players after Manchester United’s dramatic comeback against AS Roma, a message Michael Carrick’s men ought to take note of. Sensational turnaround United have made a dreadful start to the 2026/27 campaign, and their woeful sequence looked set to persist earlier this week in their meeting with Roma. The Red Devils found themselves 2-0 down inside 17 minutes, with Matías Soulé and Donyell Malen finding the back of the net. Both goals came about as a result of extremely poor defending. United received a lifeline on the hour mark via Bruno Fernandes’s penalty conversion. Having missed his initial attempt, he was granted a second bite of the apple due to an encroachment offence, and he duly made no mistake at the second time of asking. The hosts huffed and puffed and eventually restored parity in the 83rd minute when Matheus Cunha pounced on a missed clearance to fire home from close range. Cunha completed the turnaround three minutes later, connecting with a sublime pass from Shea Lacey and hammering home from a tight angle. The Brazilian was then sent off in stoppage time for a needless challenge on Leonardo Balerdi. United held on for all three points and a much-needed confidence boost. The difference between the first half and the second was immense. United appeared dead and buried in the first half, delivering a miserable performance that has become all too familiar this season. But in the second, they were almost a different side and Roma could not cope with them. This did not go unnoticed by Pressley, who observed that United simply exerted more effort and covered more ground, a message he conveyed to his players. Telling message The Dundee gaffer told The Courier , “I spoke to the group and asked them had they seen the Manchester United game.” “Because everyone loves to talk about tactics but then I watch that game and I see a team losing 2-0 at half time and what was the change?” He added, “They ran harder in the second half, they played with more energy.” “Of course tactics is important, I’m not disregarding that, but I think that we can never underestimate that if you want to win football games you have to do the basics of the game very well.” “Just now we have a league where the margins are so fine and if you don’t do the basics, if you don’t outrun your opponent, if you don’t win your duels, you don’t win games.” United are next in action on Sunday when they host Aston Villa .

item.title: Jonah Coleman continues to turn heads with the Broncos
item.description: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 01: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos runs the ball against the Kansas City Chiefs in the first quarter of a game at Empower Field At Mile High on November 01, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Jonah Coleman continues to impress. The rookie running back consistently takes advantage of the opportunities he gets on the field and runs with them, literally. In the 28-24 win over the Kansas City Chiefs, he had the game-changing reception that set up his game-winning touchdown. Now comes the next chance for Coleman on Sunday against the Carolina Panthers and their 30th-ranked rushing defense. When Broncos head coach Sean Payton was asked how Coleman has impressed despite the injury, Payton said: “We had those glimpses in the spring and in training camp and in the preseason. Atlanta, there’s a run, it just stood out to you. So the one thing that was unique about him is oftentimes you don’t get to see them in third-down protection plans, but he was someone that we had quite a bit of tape on. Advanced protection plans, and he’s built to handle the blitz. “It’s one thing to know who I have, but then also to be strong enough to do it. I would say that there were three backs — we just saw one of them that we really had visions for. Each one may be a little differently, but his versatility, to your point, that doesn’t always — you don’t get to stamp that with a lot of rookie backs that you feel like they’re going to develop into. We saw enough that we felt like he was going to be a good third-down protecting back as well, with the way he was built.” In the victory over Kansas City, Coleman finished with 11 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown, as well as four receptions for 63 yards. Obviously, that total is boosted by the 51-yard reception to put Denver on the 4-yard line. But it’s clear the rookie brings an element to this offense that the other running backs on the roster cannot. Coleman has shown great vision, instincts, and runs with physicality that is fun to watch. “I think he’s playing really well with confidence,” Broncos quarterback Bo Nix said to the media. “He’s a very intelligent young running back. What sticks out the most is he can handle a lot. You can put a lot on his plate. After we learned that R.J. Harvey wasn’t going to play last week, he got a little bit more of the bulk of R.J.’s stuff. “It’s impressive to see him be able to be used in a lot of different ways. When he gets in there, he’s a natural runner. That’s what he’s drafted for. That’s the position he plays. It’s the out-of-the-backfield stuff that I think is making a good impression on us right now.” What’s most impressive is how Coleman is handling pass protection. That’s one of the toughest aspects for a rookie running back to grasp. What’s exciting to contemplate is that Coleman can get even better the more he plays. “We caught him in the right pressure there,” Payt

item.title: Women head to north east for league meeting against Durham Cestria
item.description: Women head to north east for league meeting against Durham Cestria FA WNL Division One North action awaits Leeds United Women and Durham Cestria on Sunday, as the two sides face off at Shildon AFC. The trip north east for the Whites follows a rearranged FA Cup fixture against Rotherham United Women, in which Simon Wood's side emerged victorious. Ava Spencer-Smith broke the deadlock against a stubborn Rotherham defence, before captain Shauna Legge scored her first goal of the campaign to book a place in the Second Round, where Leeds will host Norton & Stockton Ancients. The Whites' last league outing came in midweek prior to the cup fixture, when they held off a late comeback from visitors York City Ladies to run out 4-3 winners. Alayna Millard opened the scoring before Amy Woodruff bagged a brace to return to the top of the goalscoring charts, while Brittany Sanderson guaranteed all three points late on. Durham currently sit seventh in the league standings, having drawn 0-0 away at Chester-le-Street Town Ladies before most recently suffering a 3-0 defeat to Derby County Women in the FA WNL Plate. With 12 points separating the two sides, the Whites will be keen to continue their league-topping form in County Durham on Sunday. Action from Shildon AFC gets underway at 2pm. The view from inside the camp: Ahead of the return to league action, defender Emily Cassidy said: "We've had a nice break from league action and preparations are going well. "I think we expect them to be young and a good, talented footballing side. We had two very difficult games against them last year, so we know it will be difficult." Read the full interview here . Last time on the road... Supporter Information: Sunday's game kicks off at 2pm at Shildon AFC's Dean Street, Shildon, DL4 1EZ. Tickets are priced at £6 for adults, with children and concessions charged £1. Parking is available at 14 Dean Street, DL4 1DU, and Shildon Civic Hall, DL4 1AH. Please keep up to date with the Whites by following @LUFCWomen on X, Instagram and Facebook. How to follow: For those unable to attend Sunday's match, you can stay right here on leedsunited.com to follow updates throughout the 90 minutes in our match centre. Shortly after full-time, a match report, reaction from the players and manager, along with highlights, will be available across our social media channels and website.

item.title: Bengals News: Salute to Landon Robinson
item.description: It’s November, which means two things when the Cincinnati Bengals are concerned. One: Joe Burrow and the offense have woken up from their annual offseason slumber (that extended a little too far into the season, as usual). And two: it’s Salute to Service Month. With Veterans Day just a few days away, the NFL is in its military-appreciation month, and the Bengals happen to have a defensive tackle from the Navy and a Marine on the roster. After being named the Bengals’ Salute to Service Award nominee , Landon Robinson spoke with Bengals.com’s Geoff Hobson about his time at Navy, his service, and his future before the team left for Spain. The Bengals selected Robinson with the No. 226 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. That’s the same pick the Arizona Cardinals spent on former NFL safety and former Army Ranger Pat Tillman. “I took a class where we did a case study on him [Tillman] and learned about his story and what he did in the NFL and made the decision to go serve. When I saw I got drafted 226, ‘Wow, that is crazy,’” he said when he was asked about the coincidence by Hobson. You can read the entire interview here . Here’s what else is going on: DJ Turner, key Bengals get injury updates from Madrid Quite a week for Turner, the No. 1 cornerback who appeared to suffer a serious injury just one week ago. Just having that type of player at the game would be great to see.” HOW THE BENGALS ARE TACKLING A TEST OF LOGISTICS, ROUTINE IN MADRID “One above all is keeping the schedule as close to our routine as possible,” Taylor said. “We’ve got a team of people that logistically have handled this for us that are top-notch. item.title: 'We've built on last season' - pre-Durham thoughts from Emily Cassidy
item.description: 'We've built on last season' - pre-Durham thoughts from Emily Cassidy Leeds United Women defender Emily Cassidy says the squad will be "working hard in training to prepare for league action again" as the Whites prepare to travel north east to County Durham. Facing Durham Cestria in the FA WNL Division One North, Leeds will be looking to build on consecutive victories over York City Ladies and Rotherham United Women in the league and FA Cup respectively. "We've had a nice break from league action and preparations are going well," the central defender explained. "I think we expect them to be young and a good, talented footballing side. We had two very difficult games against them last year, so we know it will be difficult. "A win would be very important as we want to keep the momentum going and start on the front foot. We have been starting games strongly this season, so starting the game well will give us confidence from the off. "It would be another step towards our goal for the season, and carrying on our winning streak would give us a boost after some tough games recently." Reflecting on the team's performances this campaign, Cassidy highlighted the strength of the squad and the progress made since last season. "I think as a team we have been very strong, aggressive and hard-working. We've built on what we wanted to improve from last season and got a style of play now which is working for us. "We also have a great squad, so the impact from the bench has been massive. "It would be amazing to get the three points and keep putting pressure on other teams around us." item.title: How artificial turf fields are affecting outdoor practices under new UIL heat safety rules
item.description: Boerne High School football players run a drill during the first day of football practice at Boerne ISD Stadium in Boerne on Monday, Aug. 3, 2026. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) A s the sun's rays beam down on the surface of Ranger Stadium, the Smithson Valley freshman football team gets ready to head to the field. While Smithson Valley's varsity squad practices outside in the mornings, freshmen practice begins at 3:30 p.m. To comply with UIL's heat safety rules, including the new wet-bulb globe temperature (WBGT) rule that went into effect in August, Smithson Valley head coach Larry Hill has occasionally modified how his freshmen practice. "Sometimes it's as simple as moving it from the turf to the grass because the temperature over there is obviously cooler," Hill said. "Other times, even on the grass it's too hot. So you know whether it's taking breaks or practice in shorts, [we'll do] whatever the mandate calls for." Escaping the heat This is the third story in a multi-part series on the UIL's new mandatory requirement of wet-bulb globe temperature (WBGT) measurements as part of an effort to combat heat across the state. Next: How a few districts are moving junior high games to the winter to protect their students While moving practice from an artificial turf field to a natural grass field does keep players cooler, why is that the case? "High schools are now switching to sport turf, and the underlying surface of sport turf oftentimes is ground-up automobile tires, so black and rubber, and it gets hot, and it radiates that heat back up onto the participant," Dr. Bud Cooper, clinical professor emeritus in the University of Georgia's department of kinesiology Cooper said. "So you know, we have to be really concerned about that." The ground absorbs heat and reflects it back onto the person, Cooper added. That's why standing outside on a grass lawn in the summer doesn't feel as hot as standing on a black asphalt parking lot. A study conducted by Penn State University in 2004 found that under direct sunlight exposure, surface temperatures of synthetic turf can be significantly higher than that of natural grass, sometimes as much as 35 to 55 degrees hotter. But just by using WBGT readings, schools are technically already taking surface heat conditions into account. Cooper explained WBGT readings factor in black globe, or radiant heat, temperatures. "That's the effects of the sun on your surroundings," Cooper said. While most schools in the San Antonio area utilize turf fields for practices and games, the coaches and band directors that spoke to the Express-News said abiding by WBGT regulations has yet to prevent them from practicing outside, even in the afternoons. "It hasn't affected us very much in the afternoon with the freshmen," Madison head coach Myles Duelm said. item.title: Commute: The SLU vs. Mizzou matchup just got more interesting
item.description: A judge cleared Robbie Avila to play. Cream Abdul-Jabbar. Larry Blurred. Milk Chamberlain. The many nicknames of the fan favorite throughout college hoops. Here’s more from Mid-Major Madness : Robbie Avila has been granted an injunction for a fifth year of eligibility by St. Louis Circuit Court Judge Jason Sengheiser. The injunction, placed on Thursday, also prohibits the NCAA from enforcing its enshrined roster limits to keep Avila, the 2026 Atlantic 10 Player of the Year, from playing for Saint Louis University. Saint Louis head coach Josh Schertz told Mid-Major Madness in the wake of the injunction that Avila “will be dressing and available for sure” for Saint Louis’ matchup with in-state rival Missouri on Friday night at the Enterprise Center. Avila’s situation is almost identical to Mark Mitchell’s. He played four seasons in four years, and was seeking a court allowance to rejoin the Billikens roster. Like Mitchell, he also played in the NBA Summer League, but never signed a contract with an NBA club. And like Mitchell, he was the best player on an NCAA Tournament team last season. Both Josh Schertz and Dennis Gates built their teams thinking they would not have either Avila or Mitchell, but given the chance to run it back with your best guy from a year ago, and a more seasoned and talented roster, it’s hard to turn down. If anything, it makes tonights game more intriguing. Avila is a terrific shooter and adept passer, but he’s slow footed and not very athletic. His basketball IQ is excellent, so you shouldn’t underestimate him. Just put him in enough situations where he has to defend quicker and more athletic guys, and attack the rim. Simple, right? Yesterday at Rock M and Rock M+ It was a quiet day yesterday. There was no game action, but today things start to heat up. Games today: Mizzou Tennis is playing in the June Stewart Invite in Nashville to close out the fall schedule. Mizzou Basketball, both Men and Women play tonight. The men are in St. Louis to take on SLU, the women travel to Little Rock to play UALR. Both games tip at 7pm. Also at 7, Volleyball takes on Texas at Hearnes. The race for the CFP responded to the first rankings being released, so Sammy’s updated post is a response to those rankings : With the Irish ranked No. 11 in the first CFP rankings, the selection committee clearly isn’t impressed with the lack of quality wins. Notre Dame has a statement opportunity on Saturday night vs Miami (FL) — as ND is 7.5-point favorites in South Bend. Notre Dame is definitely one of the more curious teams to watch. They’re really good, but the loss to BYU exposed their lack of quality on the schedule. They’ll have a big chance up against Miami this weekend but if they don’t win it’s hard seeing a path to the playoff. Another reason why they need to join a real league. Best Bets? (is anyone keeping track of Nathan’s record ATS?) More like Beamer Believer! I think it truly is a sign of the apocalypse, but I’m picking a Shane Beamer team

item.title: Washington Commanders vs LA Rams Week 9: Five Questions with Turf Show Times
item.description: INGLEWOOD, CA -DECEMBER 17: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (9) stands in the pocket to deliver a pass during third quarter action against the Washington Commanders at SoFi Stadium on December 17, 2023. (Photo by Jonathan Newton/The Washington Post via Getty Images) It’s week 9 of the NFL season and the 2-4-1 Washington Commanders will be facing a 4-4 Rams team at home at Northwest Stadium on Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET. The Rams started the season hyped as the best team in the NFL and presented as likely Super Bowl winners, but have struggled with consistency since then. At the same time, the Rams are a talented and well-coached team, having blown out the Giants 28-6 in Week 2 and the Chargers 24-9 last week. On offense, the Rams are coached by head coach Sean McVay, offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase, and assistant HC Kliff Kingsbury, with McVay calling the plays. Two of those three coaches should be familiar to Washington fans as they were former playcallers here. This offense is built around one of the NFL’s best offensive lines , a gap-scheme run game that favors power, and the NFL’s highest use of 3-TE sets . It’s an offense that sets up to bludgeon opposing defenses in the run game, but also uses their heavy personnel tendency to force opposing defenses to go heavy and set up star WR Puka Nacua to feast on heavier, slower defensive matchups. This kind of offense funnels the ball to Nacua, who currently leads the NFL with a 37.9% target share . A ruptured hamstring by WR Davante Adams will only increase the likelihood of the Rams going heavy and throwing the ball to Nacua. Overall, the Rams have the 3rd-ranked passing offense and the 6th-ranked rushing offense in terms of yards per game. On defense, the Rams have been led by DC Chris Shula, who has worked his way up from being the assistant linebackers coach of the Rams in 2017. Shula has typically employed a 3-4 front with heavy use of zone coverage on the backend, though he is also known for extensive use of disguise, both on his pressure packages (faking a blitz from one direction while actually bringing pressure from another), and in his coverage (rotating coverages post-snap to confuse QBs). This year, after the Rams traded a 1st-round pick for shutdown CB Trent McDuffie, they have occasionally been using him to shadow star WRs, which allowed him to erase Malik Nabers in their Week 2 matchup. However, McDuffie’s status is uncertain this week after sustaining a back injury against the Chargers. The Rams also just lost star CB Jaylen Watson to a season-ending shoulder injury, which could leave the backend of the Rams defense weakened. At the same time, Los Angeles may be getting back star pass rusher Myles Garrett this week, which would be a tremendous boon for their defense. Overall, the Rams have run one of the NFL’s best defenses this year by many metrics, though it has ranked better against the pass (7th) than run (15th) . item.title: Blue Jays’ Future Hall Of Famer Max Scherzer Sends Return Update
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL - MAY 04: Max Scherzer #31 of the Toronto Blue Jays takes the field prior to the game between the Toronto Blue Jays and the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on Monday, May 4, 2026 in St. Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Alex Zadorozny/MLB Photos via Getty Images) MLB Photos via Getty Images Before next season begins, the Toronto Blue Jays have several important decisions to make as regarding the rotation. After trading away Kevin Gausman and with a free agent decision looming over Shane Bieber, the team is likely to bolster the pitching staff with another arm. That could push the team to strike a reunion with future Hall of Fame righty Max Scherzer, unless he hangs up his spikes first. Shortly before his final start for the Blue Jays in this past season, Scherzer told reporters that he was not sure whether he would seek to continue his career and that he wouldn’t rush into a decision. “If he pitches, he could join a team in camp or even kick it down the road a bit longer, waiting for the perfect situation early in the season or midway through,” Keegan Matheson wrote for MLB.com at the time. “For now, Scherzer insists that this is all still up in the air.” Now Scherzer has provided his first update on his pitching plans since the season ended. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Yankees’ 25-Year-Old Depth Pitcher Cuts Ties With Team After Major Injury Toronto Blue Jays Free Agent Max Scherzer Sends Return Update Ahead Of Potential MLB Lockout On Thursday, Scherzer indicated that a return is still on the table as he detailed his workout plans for an inevitable labor lockout next month. “Future Hall of Famer Max Scherzer, 42, might keep pitching, and if his boffo finale in Toronto on short rest is any indication, there’s more there,” according to the New York Post’s Jon Heyman . “He tells The Post he plans to pitch in ‘lockout games’ near his Florida home, which will give him a better idea if season 20 will happen.” FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Blue Jays Respond To Anthony Santander’s Anti-Muslim Social Media Posts Toronto Blue Jays Could Reunite With Max Scherzer Following Lockout Announcement Although his time with the Blue Jays has included some injury setbacks, Scherzer’s contributions to the team’s postseason run in 2025 helped cement his place in the organization’s recent history. Now, as the veteran considers whether he has another season left in him, a potential MLB labor dispute could provide an unusual opportunity to test that possibility. And his latest comments suggest that his playing career might not be finished just yet. Assuming his performance in the lockout games goes well, in the same form with which he finished the season, Scherzer could appeal to the Blue Jays as a mid-rotation reunion. It would also help cement his Hall of Fame case shortly before he is inducted. According to MLB.com, he also entered his final scheduled start of the 2026 regular season with 3,550 career strikeouts, ninth on baseball’s all-time leaderboard.

item.title: Iowa Hawkeyes Football: Northwestern Wildcats Game Preview
item.description: This Saturday, the 6-2 Iowa Hawkeyes travel to the new Ryan Field to take on the surprisingly competitive 6-2 Northwestern Wildcats. The winner of this matchup keeps their (slim) playoff hopes alive while the loser will be left with a consolation-prize bowl game. Iowa beat Michigan, but even though I think Michigan played Iowa well, my opinion doesn’t count, and the Michigan win won’t impress the playoff committee. Wisconsin is good…on defense. Washington and Iowa State: eh. Looking forward, Illinois and Purdue aren’t impressive and Nebraska…well, I wouldn’t get my hopes up. That means this is Iowa’s last chance for a statement win. With a win in Evanston, the Hawks have a shot, albeit a distant one, of making the playoffs. Everything is on the line, but then again, everything was on the line in Minnesota too. 3 Questions Can Iowa Contain Aidan Chiles? Aidan Chiles is one of two quarterbacks on Iowa’s schedule that it has faced before—the other was Drake Lindsay—although when the Hawkeyes played Chiles, he was playing for Michigan State. That was in 2024 at which time Chiles had all the talent in the world but was highly inconsistent. Except against Iowa in which he had his best game of 2024 and Iowa lost a game it had no business losing to a MSU team that finished 5-7. Fast forward two years and Aidan Chiles is now a Wildcat and is the model of efficiency and consistency. He is currently completing 68.8% of his passes for 9.4 yards-per-attempt. He has thrown 13 touchdowns to 1 interception. He has also rushed for 274 yards, 10 touchdowns and 3.2 yards-per-carry. He is, after OSU’s Julian Sayin, the best quarterback Iowa will face this season. He might even be better than Sayin; Chiles is more dynamic, and he doesn’t have a safety valve named Jeremiah Smith. To make matters worse, NU boasts a strong rushing attack that will keep defenses honest, two very good tight ends, and the top wide receiver, Griffin Wilde, has 44 receptions and is averaging a whopping 17.3 yards-per-catch. In short, Iowa can’t just spy Chiles and hope that takes care of it. The Cats scored 23 points against Indiana, the best defense they have faced. Those 23 points were the most anyone, including Ohio State, has scored on the Hoosiers this year. It is worth noting that Northwestern was getting shut out until the second half. In the first half, the Hoosiers limited the big plays, kept everything in front of them and didn’t let Chiles out of the pocket. In the second half, to put it bluntly, they didn’t do those things. It’s a standard Phil Parker gameplan. Make them drive the field. Don’t let them get the big plays. Keep the quarterback in the pocket. Tighten up in the red zone. Iowa is unlikely to shut down the Cats’ high-powered offense, but if they can limit it, make them settle for field goals, win the field-position battle, and the offense can do its part then the Hawks can walk out of Evanston with a win. item.title: Drake Maye’s early-season turnaround earns him October honors
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 01: Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots throws a pass against the Miami Dolphins during the first half of the game at Hard Rock Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye was named AFC Offensive Player of the Month for October. The award comes after Maye led the Patriots to a 3-1 record, completing 67.2% of his passes for 1,199 yards, 12 touchdowns and just two interceptions. He also added 129 yards and two touchdowns on the ground. Maye became the first Patriot to earn the honor since Tom Brady during the 2017 season. “That’s something to be proud of for Drake,” Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels said. “I always look at those things as team achievements. Certainly nobody’s going to win an individual award in football without all the guys that do their jobs around him. I think you celebrate that as a group. “He’s certainly deserving of it, and a lot of credit to him for just kind of improving as September finished and got into the next month of the season. A lot of little things he did better, and hopefully we can continue to do that.” It marked a significant turnaround for Maye after the 24-year-old struggled to open the season. The quarterback was perhaps the biggest reason the Patriots found themselves with a 1-2 record through the first three weeks, throwing just one touchdown against six interceptions. Improved ball security has been one of the biggest factors in Maye’s resurgence. He has thrown just one interception over the last four weeks, while his 1.2% turnover-worthy play rate in October ranked third among qualified quarterbacks. Additionally, Maye’s trademark deep ball has returned despite the Patriots losing several of their top pass catchers to injuries, while has has operated as one of the league’s better quarterbacks when dealing with pressure. “He has worked really diligently for two years now on becoming a better passer from the pocket,” McDaniels said. “Everybody talks about how his athleticism is, and it’s great, and he made another great play outside the pocket last week. But I’d say he’d probably be more excited about the one that he slid to the right and climbed up into the pocket, and makes the throw down the field to Kyle [Williams]. So I think he’s worked really hard at it. “I think it’s repetition and I think it’s confidence in the protections. I think that’s where it stems from.” Maye’s November started strong as well as he scored three total touchdowns to lead a come from behind win in Miami. The quarterback will look to keep things going against the Green Bay Packers this Sunday.

item.title: 4-billion-year-old 'Rosetta Stone' found in Sahara Desert could unlock the secret history of water on Mars
item.description: null A rose-colored rock discovered in the Sahara Desert may hold some clues to Mars' ancient geological history. The meteorite , named Teghaza 001 after the salt plain in Mali where it was discovered in 2022, weighs roughly 1.8 pounds (800 grams) and formed more than 4.1 billion years ago. Blasted off Mars by an impact before eventually landing on Earth, it is one of the three oldest Martian meteorites ever found. The extraordinary age and unusual mineral composition of Teghaza 001 offer a rare glimpse into the formation of Mars' early crust and how volcanic materials may have been altered by water, according to a statement from NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. "It was only after we started looking closely that we realized this meteorite is really unique,” research leader Yang Liu of NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California said in the statement. "One of the paper’s reviewers called it a Rosetta Stone for Mars." A Rosetta Stone for Mars Unlike many Martian meteorites, Teghaza 001 contains a distinctive combination of igneous minerals and textures that preserve evidence of its complex history. Its mineral composition resembles materials observed in Mars' southern highlands by NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter . Although researchers can’t pinpoint exactly where the meteorite originated on Mars, they have identified 13 potential locations on the planet where it may have formed. "This is really our first piece of Martian crust from a part of Mars we’ve never had a sample of before," team member Lee Saper, NASA’s Ames Research Center in Silicon Valley, said. "It records interactions of water and rock and maybe even an imprint of the Martian atmosphere as it was losing water." The meteorite was initially identified as Martian based on its oxygen isotopes. To determine its age, scientists then examined tiny zircon crystals embedded in the rock. Using a specialized rubidium-strontium dating technique, researchers analyzed individual mineral grains on its surface, preserving it for future analysis. 13 locations on Mars that match the mineralogy and chemistry of Teghaza 001, one of the most ancient Martian meteorites ever found on Earth (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/USGS) The results revealed that Teghaza 001 was altered by water around 4.1 billion years ago, suggesting the rock itself formed even earlier. The mineral and chemical evidence points to a dynamic water cycle on ancient Mars, when liquid water interacted with the planet's crust and potentially left traces of its atmosphere as it gradually lost water. Scientists believe further analysis of Teghaza 001 could reveal more about how water shaped the Martian surface and influenced the planet's evolution. The study also marks the first time researchers have used rubidium-strontium dating to analyze an ancient Martian meteorite , opening the door for the technique to be applied to other samples in the future. "We've only scratched the surface," Liu concluded.

item.title: UK ministers seek powers to investigate when AI agents are let off the leash
item.description: The UK government is paving the way for rules requiring essential service operators and digital providers to guard against losing control of AI agents and report incidents when safeguards fail. An amendment to the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, which is passing through Parliament , would give ministers powers to regulate the deployment and reporting of agentic AI in certain organizations. The new clause was introduced during the bill's third reading in the House of Lords this week. In an explanatory note , ministers outlined plans for safeguards, notification of affected organizations, preservation of evidence, and government-led incident reviews. The measures would require consultation and parliamentary approval through secondary legislation. The move follows a series of incidents. Last month, OpenAI revealed that its agents repeatedly strayed beyond their intended scope , prompting the company to notify more than 100 organizations about the issues. That came after July's incident, in which an OpenAI agent accessed the internet and breached machine learning platform Hugging Face . The episode, and the potential for more damage from poorly designed AI agent deployments, have prompted MPs to question whether UK law can deal with such threats. Speaking to The Register , Stuart Davey, a partner at law firm Pinsent Masons, described the clause as "quite novel." Rather than directly imposing new duties, it would allow ministers to introduce rules and investigatory powers covering regulated organizations. Davey said that could include powers "to look where there has been such an AI agentic compromise or issue, and do some things... appoint inspectors, enter and search premises, seize and retain documents." Under the proposals, the minister could confer certain powers on regulators, requiring action from targeted organizations. Potentially affected organizations include gas and electricity suppliers, managed service providers, and cloud providers deploying AI agents for customers. Foundation model developers would not automatically fall within scope simply because they build the underlying technology. "Where there's a security or operational compromise in relation to a relevant network or information system, that would seem to capture those managed service providers or cloud computing providers who are using AI, and there's that loss of control," said Davey. He advised cloud and managed service providers to track whether the proposed measures become law. Evin McMullen, CEO and co-founder of AI identity and control infrastructure company AmanTrue, said the amendment recognizes loss of oversight or control as a security risk but does not itself impose new duties. "The amendment allows future regulations to introduce investigatory and enforcement powers where an incident involves an AI agent, targeting organizations running essential digital services," he said. item.title: UK-based OBIMI Brings Families Together in Lagos to Support Children With Disabilities
item.description: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Its founder, Helen Ewumi , is a qualified social worker and a parent of children with disabilities. Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone. The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma. Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families. During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included. The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. As a social worker and a parent with lived experience of caring for children with disabilities, she understands how important it is for families to feel listened to and supported. OBIMI CIC is grateful to the families, school staff, volunteers, partners and supporters who helped make the outreach possible. The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included. About The Founder OBIMI founder Helen Ewumi at the Nigeria outreach in Lagos. A UK-based social worker and parent of children with disabilities, Helen founded OBIMI to support families and challenge disability stigma. item.title: King Charles’ Birthday: UK reaffirms commitment to stronger Nigeria ties
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The British High Commissioner to Nigeria, Mr Pete Vowles, has reaffirmed the United Kingdom’s commitment to strengthening bilateral relations with Nigeria, describing the partnership between both countries as dynamic, reciprocal and ambitious. Vowles stated this on Thursday in Abuja at an event organised to celebrate the 78th birthday of His Majesty, King Charles III, and the longstanding relationship between the United Kingdom and Nigeria. Speaking on the theme of the celebration, GREAT, the High Commissioner said it reflected the strength of the relationship and the opportunities available for both countries to expand their cooperation. He said the partnership was exceptional in its content and continued to evolve in response to changing times, while maintaining mutual respect and equality. He said, “Well, we thought Great was a good way to talk about the great partnership that we have between the UK and Nigeria. A partnership that is exceptional in its content, but also I think it’s a partnership that is dynamic, it’s a partnership that is reciprocal, it’s a partnership that is ambitious.” Explaining the theme further, Vowles said, “And I say that because dynamic means it’s constantly evolving to the changing times. Reciprocal because it’s respectful, it’s two-way, it treats each other as equals. And ambitious because we know there is so much more we can do together.” The High Commissioner, expressed his determination to build on the progress recorded in relations between both countries, particularly following President Bola Tinubu’s state visit to the United Kingdom earlier in the year. Vowles said he would work to implement the agreements reached during the visit and explore further areas of cooperation for the mutual benefit of both countries. He urged Nigerians to contribute their ideas and energy towards strengthening the relationship, noting that there was room for greater engagement between the two countries. “We work hard together but we can do even more together. So bring your energy, bring your ideas and let’s do more together,” he said. Also speaking, the Country Director of the Royal Commonwealth Society, Nigeria Branch, Mr Blackson Olaseni Bayewumi, congratulated King Charles III on his 78th birthday and wished him many more years of service to the Commonwealth. Bayewumi, who described the King as an important link between the Royal Commonwealth Society and the Commonwealth, said His Majesty was the head of the Commonwealth and patron of the society. He said his relationship with the British High Commission in Abuja dated back to 1999, following Nigeria’s return to democratic rule and readmission into the Commonwealth after its suspension during military rule. According to him, the relationship had continued through various initiatives and programmes aimed at promoting Commonwealth values in Nigeria. He listed some of the activities as the Commonwealth essay competition, Commonwealth Spiritual Classics camp

item.title: Emergency delays: Doctors reject bill proposing 6-month jail term
item.description: The Nigerian Association of Resident Doctors (NARD) has rejected proposed legislation seeking a six-month jail term or ₦300,000 fine for healthcare professionals over delays in emergency medical treatment. This is contained in a statement issued by the NARD President, Dr Ogar Idoko, in Calabar on Friday. Idoko described the proposed amendment to the National Health Act as punitive, arguing that doctors should not be criminalised for failures arising from inadequate healthcare infrastructure. He said the association recognised the importance of prompt emergency care and protecting patients but insisted that systemic challenges must be addressed before imposing criminal sanctions. According to him, doctors nationwide work under difficult conditions, including obsolete equipment, inadequate staffing, unreliable electricity and insufficient emergency medical supplies. “The challenges are consequences of longstanding institutional neglect rather than professional negligence, so I urge lawmakers to prioritise healthcare funding and infrastructure. “We also challenge the National Assembly to demonstrate similar legislative urgency in providing functional emergency departments, modern diagnostic equipment, reliable ambulance services and adequate personnel,” he said. He asserted that lawmakers should consider legislation compelling public office holders to use Nigerian government hospitals, with sanctions for misuse of public resources on avoidable overseas medical treatment. He warned that additional criminal penalties against overstretched healthcare professionals could worsen the country’s brain drain, popularly known as the “Japan syndrome.” He stated that the association acknowledged that the proposed bill reportedly contained safeguards for circumstances beyond practitioners’ control but insisted that such provisions must be explicit and enforceable. He called for the withdrawal and reconsideration of the proposed punitive provisions, alongside consultations involving healthcare associations, hospital administrators, patient representatives and other stakeholders. He urged the National Assembly to prioritise legislation guaranteeing adequate health funding, minimum emergency-care standards, appropriate staffing, constant electricity and functional referral systems. “We will consider all lawful options, including nationwide industrial action, if lawmakers proceeded with legislation unjustly criminalising doctors for institutional failures. “We however, pledged to make necessary arrangements to protect emergency and critically ill patients during any industrial action, while we reaffirm our commitment to patient safety and quality healthcare.,” he said. NAN reports that the Senate is considering a bill that seeks to punish hospitals and healthcare workers who refuse or delay emergency medical treatment.
